With the mantra, "You are invigorating, subduers of Vṛtra," he consecrates the waters while they are being replenished; with the mantra, "O Soma, that light of yours which is in heaven," he consecrates the two pressing-boards. With the mantra, "O two Dhiṣaṇās, being firm, do you make yourselves firm," [he addresses them]. The pressing-stone is above, and the skin-bag is below. Then, while pouring [the water] clockwise around the Hotṛ’s cup, he performs the *nigrābha* rite with the mantra, "Let the quarters—east, west, north, and south—run toward you; O Mother, flow down. He touches the six skin-bags.

The pressing-stones become closely joined and moist. 5. Raising the pressing-stone, they say: "Do not fear; do not tremble. 6. Wherever he sees a blade of grass or a root, there he presses again, saying: "Sinless, sent by Indra, we [press] thee; may Vāyu be gracious to thee; may Mitra be gracious to thee; may Varuṇa be gracious to thee; King Soma, when struck by me, is gracious. 7. With this same formula, from that point onward, he should press. 8. Having first pressed eight times, he should press once more.

He undergoes the *nigrābha* [sprinkling] twice, either at the beginning or at the end. He undergoes the *nigrābha* four times; it is known from the tradition that he draws [the water] upward three times with the ladle and then pours it out. Having taken the shoots that have been seized, the Pratiprasthātṛ covers them with two shoots and holds them up toward the north. Taking the King [Soma] with his joined palms, the Adhvaryu leads him to the *upāṃśu* vessel with the mantra: "O vigorous one, flow pure for Vācaspati. Two other pressings are performed in this same manner. Alternatively, he may press a second time eleven times and a third time twelve times. 13.10

The Pratiprasthātṛ covers the vessel with two other pure [strainers]. Without setting down the cup, the Adhvaryu takes it and rises, saying: "Thou art consecrated by thy own self; make our nourishments honey-sweet. He carries it to the north of the Hotṛ, saying: "Follow along the wide atmosphere. They both stand by the northern junction of the enclosing sticks, saying: "May the mind attend thee. Standing upright, facing south-eastward, he offers continuously, saying: "Svāhā! Thee, O well-born one, for Sūrya!"—[and] "Thee for the gods."

Having offered with the formula, "To the Marīcipas," he wipes the residue onto the enclosing stick (paridhi). (6) If he should desire, "May Parjanya be rainy," he should wipe it with the palm turned downwards. (7) If he should desire, "May he be non-rainy," he should wipe it with the palm turned upwards. (8) Having poured the residue into the Āgrayaṇa vessel, he places the cup in its proper place with the formula, "This is thy womb; for out-breathing, thee. (9) Taking one of the unpressed stalks, the Adhvaryu throws it into the Upāṃśu cup.

They remain lying there until the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*). Then, having become dry, he mixes them with water, [reciting]: "O Soma, that name of yours which is invincible and wakeful. Two by two, or at each pressing, if he should wish to practice sorcery against someone, he should take the *upāṃśu* cup and set it down, saying: "I set thee down upon the breath of so-and-so. Then, having taken it with the *sāvitra* formula, he carries it forward. This is the same up to the offering. When about to offer, he consecrates it, saying: "Slay so-and-so; then I shall offer thee. If [the person] should be far away, he should stand [over the fire] until darkness falls. Having stirred [the oblation], he offers it.
"In the exhilaration of the intoxicating drink that causes great joy, may this [offering] be false; svāhā! 17. The rest is the same. 18. 13.11.

He pours the greater part of the King [Soma] onto the pressing-skin; he leaves a smaller portion remaining for the midday pressing. Having mixed it with the Vasatīvarī waters and reached the *nigrābha* formula, they press the Soma an unlimited number of times. They reach the *nigrābha*; they press; they reach the *nigrābha*. They press [the Soma]; having poured the thrice-pressed King [Soma] together into a cup, he pours it into the *ādhavanīya* vessel. Two others are prepared in the same manner. At the final pressing, having squeezed out the *ṛjīṣa*, they make the King [Soma] well-prepared. Having wiped it with a strainer, he squeezes it. Having placed the pressing-stones facing each other upon the skin for pressing, he removes the *ṛjīṣa* from the stones.

He makes them have the *ṛjīṣa* as their mouth. (10) The Udgātṛs place the *droṇakalaśa* upon the pressing-stones facing east. (11) They draw it forward along the axle. (12) Over the *droṇakalaśa*, they spread the filter (*pavitra*) with its fringes pointing north. (13) Having consecrated the King Soma with the mantra: "Thy filter is spread, O Brahmaṇaspati; thou, the lord, encompassest the limbs on every side. He whose body is not heated by penance, being raw, does not partake of that; only those who are cooked [by fire] and carry it have attained it," the sacrificer causes a continuous stream to flow from the Hotṛ’s cup through the filter. He should interrupt the stream for one whom he hates. (14) 13.12

With water, the Unnetṛ pours from the Ādhavanīya vessel into the Hotṛ’s cup. Across the filter, he draws the Antaryāma cup from the flowing stream with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; O Maghavan, restrain within. Its ritual procedure is explained by that of the Upāṃśu cup; there is only this much difference.

He carries [the cup] to the south of the Hotṛ or to the north. (4) With the words, "May the mind attend thee," they both settle down along the southern junction of the enclosing sticks. (5) Standing straight, facing eastward and then northward, he offers continuously with the formula, "Svāhā! Thee, O well-born one, to Sūrya! (6) The smearing, wiping, and pouring of the remnants have been explained. (7) He places the Antaryāma vessel in its place like a cook's vessel with the formula, "This is thy womb; for out-breathing, thee! (8) If he should practice sorcery, he should say over the Antaryāma vessel: "I place thee in the out-breathing of so-and-so."

Having taken [the cup], he should set it down; 9 the rest is the same. 10 Between those two, he sets down the Upāṃśusavana stone so that it touches [the cups] with the formula: "For the diffused breath (vyāna) thee! 11 If he should practice sorcery, he should set down the Upāṃśusavana stone with the formula: "I set thee down for the diffused breath of so-and-so! 12 Thus they remain set down until the third pressing. 13 He should offer both of them after sunrise if he is not in a hurry. 14 But if he is in a hurry, he should offer the Upāṃśu before sunrise.

Some prescribe the offering of the Upāṃśu and Antaryāma cups when [the sun] has risen; others prescribe the offering of the Upāṃśu and Antaryāma cups in the reverse order. Some say both should be offered before sunrise. 13.13. He draws the cups with a stream flowing across the filter. If the Soma sacrifice has the *Rathantara* as its *sāman*, he should draw the cups beginning with the Aindravāyava. If it has the *Bṛhat* as its *sāman*, [he should draw them] beginning with the Śukra. If it has the *Jagat* as its *sāman*, [he should draw them] beginning with the Āgrayaṇa. If it has both *sāmans*, he should draw [them] beginning with the Aindravāyava. "One who suffers from illness should draw [them] beginning with the Aindravāyava"—these optional rules regarding the sequence of the cups are explained in the Brāhmaṇa.

The cups indeed begin with those for Indra and Vāyu (aindravāyava). 3. If one should take any other optional cup (kāmya-graha) prior to the one for Indra and Vāyu, he should hold it until the setting down of the cup for Indra and Vāyu. 4. Then, having set down that cup for Indra and Vāyu, he should set down [the others]. 5. Those cups which he takes prior to the Āgrayaṇa, he should take them "with water" (upāṃśu); those which are subsequent to it, he should take them "with a support" (upabdimat). 6. When taking the cups beginning with the Āgrayaṇa, having taken the Manthin cup, he should release his speech.

When drawing the cups beginning with the Ukthya, he should draw the Upām̐śu-ukthya. 7. He draws the Aindravāyava cup, beginning with "O Vāyu, come hither, O drinker of the pure," and ending with "Thou art taken with a support; for Vāyu, thee! 8. Having moved the vessel aside, he draws it again, beginning with "Indra and Vāyu, these [Somas] are pressed," and ending with "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra and Vāyu, thee! 9. Then, having wiped it with a strainer, he places it in its proper place with "This is thy womb; for the two who are in harmony, thee! 10.

In this very same way, having drawn the other cups according to their respective deities, he deposits them in their proper places with their respective formulas of settling. Whenever the formula for settling might not be explicitly prescribed, he should settle it with the words, "This is thy womb.
He draws the cup for Mitra and Varuṇa with the verse, "O Mitra and Varuṇa, this [is for you]... Then he mixes it with warm milk that has been boiled, [reciting]:
"May we, having come together, rejoice in wealth; may the gods [rejoice] in our oblation, as cows in pasture."
O Mitra and Varuna, bestow upon us that cow forever, one that never falters.

Thus [he concludes]. Having passed over the Āśvina cup, he draws the Śukra cup with the verse: "This Vena has impelled those born from the speckled womb. (3) Then he mixes it with gold, saying: "I mix your bright [juice] with the bright [gold]. (4) Thereafter, he draws the Manthin cup with the verse: "As of old, as of former times... (5) Then he mixes it with barley meal, [reciting]:
"O you two who, like the mind, in these invocations, with your power, win sharp inspired songs as swift steeds;
may he, the one of many heroic deeds, who reaches with his arrows, mix this [meal] from his hand. (6)

Thus, having caused himself and the other cups to resound, he then draws the Āgrayaṇa in two streams. Having poured that King [Soma] which is in the Āgrayaṇa vessel into another vessel, he makes the second stream with the verse: "O gods who are eleven in heaven... He should draw it for one who has enemies with a verse containing the word *rugṇa* (broken), namely: "The thirty and the three groups, breaking down... Having drawn the Āgrayaṇa, having uttered the *hiṃ* sound three times, he releases his speech with: "Soma purifies itself; Soma..."

"Soma flows; he flows for this *brahman*, he flows for this *kṣatra*, he flows for this people (*viś*), he flows for this presser, the sacrificer; he flows for food, he flows for strength, he flows for the waters, he flows for the plants, he flows for the trees, he flows for heaven and earth, he flows for well-being, he flows for spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*), he flows for the sacrificer, he flows for my preeminence. Thus it is known: "He pronounces [the formula] softly first, then loudly, then very loudly. (10–11) 13.15

Then he takes three *atigrāhya* cups with these three sections: "O Agni, you purify our lives... (RV IX.66.19–21). Then [he takes] the *ukthya*: "Thou art taken with a support; for Indra, the mighty, the vigorous... Then [he takes] the *dhruva*: "The head of heaven, the messenger of earth... If he should desire of someone, "May he attain a full lifespan," for him he should take a full cup. He should place it upon gold for one who desires long life. It is known: "The prince guards the *dhruva*. When the *dhruva* has been taken...

The sacrificer does not urinate until the pouring down [of the Soma]. (7) He causes the King [Soma] to be poured through into the *droṇakalaśa* as much as he considers sufficient for the morning pressing. (8) Having squeezed the filter and spread it over the *pūtabhṛt* vessel, he distributes the *ekadhana* waters contained in the *maitrāvaruṇacamasīyā* vessels. (9) After having poured the *ekadhana* waters into the *ādhavanīya* according to their purpose, he pours a portion of the King [Soma] from the *ādhavanīya* into the *pūtabhṛt*. (10) In this regard, there is this specific instruction.

Wherever and whatever he should pour from the *pūtabhṛt*, he should pour it across the filter, except for the *droṇakalaśa*. He draws the *pavamāna* cups. He should touch the *droṇakalaśa* with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; for Prajāpati, thee! [He should touch] the *ādhavanīya* with the formula: "For Indra and Agni, thee!"

"From all the gods, thee!"—with this [formula] he draws from the *pūtabhṛt* vessel. It is known: "Those [libations] which are drawn with the *upayāma* formula before the verse, and those with the *upayāma* formula after the verse, are for the support of the sacrifice. They offer the *vaipruṣa* oblations with these three verses beginning, "Thy drop that falls. Having offered the *saptahotṛ* oblation, they proceed toward the north, bowing down, to the *bahiṣpavamāna* laud. The *prastotṛ* takes hold of the *adhvaryu*; the *udgātṛ* takes hold of the *prastotṛ*; the *pratihartṛ* takes hold of the *udgātṛ*; and the *brahmā* takes hold of the *pratihartṛ*.

The sacrificer [is] the Brahman; according to some, the Brahman [is] the sacrificer. 16. While shaking a handful of sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the Adhvaryu first creeps forward, saying: "The Gāyatra path, the Vasus as the deity; by the unobstructed path of the wolf, may I safely reach the Vasus," and also, "May Speech go at the head. 17.13.16. They sit down to the south of the *cātvāla* pit. Having sat down in front of the Prastotṛ, the Adhvaryu, while handing over the handful of sacrificial grass to the Prastotṛ, introduces the chant (*stotra*), beginning with: "Vāyu is the *hiṃ*-singer; may those gods who sustain life bestow life-breath upon me."

1. With the verse ending "Soma flows on," he introduces all the *stotra*s with this very formula. 2. He performs the action following the *pavamāna* chants elsewhere with the formula, "Turn hither! 3. They chant while looking at the *cātvāla* pit. 4. While the *stotra* is being chanted, four officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) join in the singing (*upagāyanti*). 5. They sing from the various directions. 6. The officiating priests, with the sacrificer as the fifth, join in the singing. 7. It is known from tradition that the *adhvaryu* should not join in the singing. 8. Other officiating priests join in the singing with the syllable "Oṃ."

"Ho!"—thus the sacrificer [responds]. 9. While the chant is being performed, the sacrificer mutters the formula for ascending after it: "Thou art a falcon, having the Gāyatrī as thy metre. 10. He addresses the one who has been praised with the formula: "Of the praised, thou art the praise. 11. By this same formula, he addresses all the *stotras*. 12. Having been praised, while rising, he says: "O Āgnīdhra, distribute the fires; spread the sacrificial grass (*barhis*); prepare the sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśas*); O Pratiprasthātṛ, come to the animal victim. 13. Having returned, the sacrificer worships the King (Soma) with the verse: "O Viṣṇu, thou art our nearest [kinsman]. 14.

Having brought embers from the Āgnīdhra fire, the Āgnīdhra distributes the hearths (dhiṣṇiyas) according to their respective positions. Sitting in front and facing west, the Pratiprasthātṛ pours libations over the hearths. Taking the King Soma from the Droṇakalaśa vessel with the dipping-spoon, he pours it over the Āhavanīya, the Āgnīdhrīya, and the Hotrīya hearths; the others he sprinkles with ghee taken five times.

With the *soma*, [he cleanses] the *mārjālīya* hearth. (17) Those very mantras used for the pouring out [of the grain] are also used for the sprinkling. (18) Having washed the vessels for the *savanīya* offerings, he sets them down—those which are made of plant materials. (19) Having prepared the two strainers (*pavitra*), he issues the command: "O sacrificer, restrain your speech. (20) Restraining his speech, he touches the vessels. (21) 13.17

Then he offers the *savanīya* oblations: parched grains (*dhānā*) for Indra accompanied by the *Harivant* [deities], a gruel-porridge (*karambha*) for Indra accompanied by Pūṣan, and a husked-grain mixture (*parivāpa*) for Sarasvatī Bhāratī; a cake on eight potsherds for Indra at the morning pressing, on eleven potsherds at the midday pressing, and on twelve potsherds at the third pressing—or rather, on eleven potsherds throughout. They call the gruel-porridge "mantha."

"Parched grains (lājān) with the parivāpa"—this is the same up to the pouring [of the grains]. Having sown barley and placed a potsherd for the sake of the parched grains, he pours half of the rice-grains into it, mixing them with water purified by the *yajus*-formula. While pouring, he mutters the formula used for placing [the vessel] on the fire; while removing [it from the fire], he mutters the formula used for taking it down. Having sprinkled the parched grains from the frying pan with clarified butter, he takes them down. At the proper time, he adorns [the sacrificer's wife]. This is the same up to the threshing. Having threshed the barley, he makes the parched grains free of husks with his two hands.

In this context, the mantra for sowing, the mantra for threshing, the mantra for pouring out, and the mantra for winnowing are performed; (furthermore,) the mantras for the mortar and pestle should be performed with the two hands. Then he threshes the grains intended for the *puroḍāśa*. Having performed that which precedes the sowing (*adhivapana*), he places the potsherd for the *karambha* and pours half of the barley-grains onto the potsherd for the sake of the *karambha*. The ritual purification (*saṃskāra*) has been explained. They grind the parched grains (*dhānāḥ*) according to the procedure for the flour (*piṣṭa*). It is the same up to the placing of the potsherds.

He mixes the *mantha* and the *puroḍāśa* together (1). Having poured out the parched grains (*dhānā*), he places the *puroḍāśa* on the fire (2). In the same manner, having removed the parched grains, he removes the *puroḍāśa* from the fire (3). The Āgnīdhra priest alone spreads the *barhis* grass across the back (the spine) of the altar (4). He adorns the *puroḍāśas* (5). Then he draws the cup for the Aśvins from the *droṇakalaśa* using the *pariplu* ladle, with this section beginning "The honey-sweet whip which belongs to you two" (TS 3.2.8), or with the following one (6). From the *droṇakalaśa* alone, from this point forward, he draws the cups using the *pariplu* ladle, except in other cases.

Having drawn the Āśvina cup from the *dhārāgraha* vessels and having encircled the sacrificial post with a triple-twisted cord (*trivṛt*), he dedicates the animal for Agni as the *savanīya-paśu* at the Agniṣṭoma. At the Ukthya, he dedicates a second animal for Indra-Agni. At the Ṣoḍaśin, he dedicates a third, a ram for Indra.

At the Atirātra sacrifice, he erects a ewe for Sarasvatī as the fourth [victim] (8). He erects the eleven posts measured according to the altar (9). [The ritual] is the same up to the offering of the omentum (10). When the omentum has been offered, those intending to step forward gaze at the cups (11). "Two oceans, vast and undecaying," [with these words] they look at the Droṇakalaśa and Ādhavanīya vessels (12). "Two worlds," [with these words] they look at the Pūtabhṛt vessel (13). They all stand in attendance upon the King Soma, beginning with "He who encompasses Agni, he who encompasses Indra," and ending with "I wipe this of thee" (14).

"For my out-breath," [he addresses] the Upāṃśu cup; 15. "For my in-breath," the Antaryāma; 16. "For my diffused breath," the Upāṃśusavana stone; 17. "For my speech," the Aindravāyava cup; 18. "For my skill and will," the Maitrāvaruṇa cup; 19. "For my two eyes," the Śukra and Manthin cups; 20. 13.19 "For my hearing," the Āśvina cup; 1. "For my self," the Āgrayaṇa cup; 2. "For my limbs," the Ukthya cup; 3. "For my life-span," the Dhruva cup; 4. "For my splendor," "for my vigor."

With "For my splendor," he [offers] the *atigrāhya* cups; with "For my vigor," the *ṣoḍaśin* vessel, if there is a *ṣoḍaśin* sacrifice; with "Thou art the belly of Viṣṇu," the *droṇakalaśa*; with "Thou art the belly of Indra," the *ādhavanīya*; with "Thou art the belly of the All-gods," the *pūtabhṛt*. They all stand near the King (Soma) beginning with "Who art thou? What is thy name? and ending with "This I wipe for thee. One who desires prosperity should gaze [at him].

"It is known from tradition: 'One desiring spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*) should look [at them]; one who is not ill should look; one practicing sorcery (*abhicaran*) should look. (11) Thereafter, he pays homage (*upatiṣṭhate*) to the other objects. (12) On the rubbish-heap (*utkara*), he pays homage to the implements for preparing the altar with these mantras according to their respective forms: "The wooden sword (*sphya*) is well-being (*svasti*); the *vighana* is well-being. (13) And to all of them [he says]: "O you who are worthy of sacrifice (*yajñiya*) and performers of sacrifice (*yajñakṛt*), do you invite me to this sacrifice! (14) To Heaven and Earth: "May Heaven and Earth invite me! (15) To the *āstāva*: "The *āstāva*! (16) To the water-jar: "The jar (*kalaśa*)! (17)

"To Droṇakalaśa" (17); "To Soma" for the Soma-vessel (18); "To Agni" for the Āhavanīya fire (19); "Near the gods, near the sacrifice" for the sacrifice (20); "May the Hotrās call upon me in the invitation" for the Hotrakas (21); [the formulas] "let them call," "let two of them call," and "let them all call" are to be supplied as continuations (22). "Homage to Agni, the slayer of Makha" for the Āhavanīya fire (23); "Homage to Rudra, the slayer of Makha" for the Āgnīdhrīya fire (24); "Homage to Indra, the slayer of Makha" for the Hotrīya fire (25). "You two are firm; you two are relaxed; being united, protect me from injury."
"Thus may Heaven and Earth [protect me]," (26); "May the divine Sūrya protect me from the sky with his smile," thus [he addresses] the Āditya. (27) 13.20

"Vāyu from the intermediate space"—[he addresses] Vāyu; 1. "Agni from the earth"—Agni; 2. "Yama from the fathers"—Yama; 3. "Sarasvatī from men"—Sarasvatī; 4. "O divine doors, do not burn me"—the two doors of the *sadas*; 5. "Homage to the *sadas*"—the *sadas*; 6. "Homage to the lord of the *sadas*"—the sacrificer; 7. "Homage to the eye of friends who go before"—the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*); 8. "Homage to heaven"—heaven; 9. "Homage to earth"—earth; 10. Having entered [the *sadas*].

He worships that place where he is about to sit down, saying: "O son of a remarried woman, depart; sit on the seat of another who is more simple-minded than we. Having stepped across the space in front of the *praśāstrīya* shed, he sits down, saying: "May I go up from the downward slope and up from the upward slope. He gazes at heaven and earth, saying: "O Heaven and Earth, protect me this day. He should look toward the southern half of the *sadas*, saying: "Come, O Fathers! May I be rich in fathers through you; may you be rich in offspring through me."

14. Having set down the *savaniya* offerings, he issues the command: "For the morning pressing of the Soma, recite the invitatory verses for the rice-cake offerings to Indra. 15. Having spread a base of clarified butter in the *juhū* ladle, he takes portions from all the sacrificial oblations. 16. Having taken a portion from the *āmikṣā*, he takes a portion from the whey (*vājina*); or he does not take a portion from the whey. 17. Having taken the portions and sprinkled them with clarified butter, having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "For the morning pressing of the Soma, give the command for the rice-cake offerings set forth for Indra. 18. He issues the command: "Recite the invitatory verse for Agni."

"Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Agni," [he says] regarding the Sviṣṭakṛt offering. 19. Regarding this, one view is that he should cut off the iḍā portion right here; another view is that it should be from the uppermost [portion]. 20. 13.21.

Then, while they are performing the offering for the two deities, he issues the command: "Recite the invitatory verse for Indra and Vāyu. The Pratiprasthātṛ takes a portion of the draught for Indra and Vāyu with the Āditya vessel, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art seated in speech; I take thee for the two guardians of speech, the two guardians of the ritual will, the two supervisors over the firm foundation of this sacrifice. According to some, the *pratinigrāhya* cups are drawn from the *droṇakalaśa* and offered without being set down. Having taken the draught for Indra and Vāyu, the Adhvaryu [proceeds].

Having taken up the King [Soma] with the dipping-spoon from the Ṛṇa-vessel, he pours the Āghāra-libation with the mantra: "O Gods, may this sacrifice, this worship, be for the plants. Regarding this, there is this specific instruction: in the middle of the fire, he offers the oblations of clarified butter, the oblations of the animal victim, and the oblations of the sacrificial cakes.

There are six Soma-libations for the base at the beginning and the end. Standing where he thinks, "I shall offer without stepping forward," he should call for the *āśrāvaṇa* (the announcement). Having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for Vāyu and Indra-Vāyu. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered again, they both make the offering. He follows the offering with the mantra: "Thou art the yoke, the best of rays; protector of the out-breath (*prāṇa*), protect my out-breath! Thou art the yoke, the best of rays; protector of the in-breath (*apāna*), protect my in-breath! If he, being the first...

If one has a rival who seeks to overwhelm him, he should grasp his thumb with his finger while reciting: "O Indra and Vāyu, whoever seeks to harm us... (12). The Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue from the Adhvaryu’s cup into his own; the Adhvaryu pours it into the Pratiprasthātṛ’s cup. The Pratiprasthātṛ pours it into the Āditya vessel with the formula: "For the gods, thee! (13). The Adhvaryu hands the portion for consumption to the Hotṛ with the formula: "In me is Vasu, Purovasu; O Vāk, protect my speech! (14). The Hotṛ receives it with this same formula. (15) 13.22

In the same way, they proceed with the two northern [cups] according to their respective deities; this much is the difference. With the subsequent mantra, he takes the *pratinigrāhya* cup. There is no *āghāra* libation here. They both offer once each. With each subsequent [mantra], he pushes it away.

To the north, he pours each subsequent residue into the Aditya vessel. Then he covers it with that very same vessel, saying: "O Viṣṇu, stride out! This is your Soma; guard it. Let no evil-eyed one look upon it. To the north, the Adhvaryu hands over the draughts one after another; the Hotṛ receives them with each one in the same manner. He pours the contents of the Ādhavanīya vessel into the Pūtabhṛt.

Having placed the *ādhavanīya* [vessel] down, the *unnetṛ* issues the command: "Recite for the cups being filled. He fills nine cups, with the cup of the *hotṛ* as the foremost, excluding the cup of the *achāvāka*. Having made an under-layer of ghee from the *droṇakalaśa* and having drawn [Soma] from the *pūtabhṛt*, he pours over it from the *droṇakalaśa* itself. In this regard, there is this specific rule: wherever he may fill the cups, the *unnetṛ* should fill them in this very manner.

From this point onward, he draws up all the cups without exception. (9) The *unnīyamāna-sūkta* is recited only over those cups that belong to the opening of the *savana*. (10) When the *unnīyamāna-sūkta* has been completed and the chant has been performed, the Adhvaryu takes up the *śukra* cup with the formula: "Thou art praised, O sustainer of people; may the gods who drink the *śukra* lead thee forward. "Thou art praised, O sustainer of people."

"May the gods, the drinkers of the *manthin*, lead thee forth"—with these words, the Pratiprasthātṛ [takes] the *manthin*. (11) With the *Sāvitra* formula, both [priests] cover [the vessels] from above with two un-sprinkled wooden chips. (12) From below, they place two sprinkled [chips] as a protection against evil. (13) "Śaṇḍa is driven away along with so-and-so"—thus says the Adhvaryu; he utters the name of him whom he hates. (14) "Marka is driven away along with so-and-so"—thus says the Pratiprasthātṛ.
He utters the name of the one whom he hates; covering their heads with both hands, they go out toward the east, saying: "Traverse the wide atmosphere. 16. 13.23.

With the front [of the poles], they join the two cups at the *havirdhāna* sheds, or they join the two forearms: "Join the Brahman; quicken that for me! Join the Kṣatra; quicken that for me! Join the food (*iṣ*); quicken that for me! Join the strength (*ūrj*); quicken that for me! Join the wealth (*rayi*); quicken that for me! Join the prosperity (*puṣṭi*); quicken that for me! Join the progeny (*prajā*); quicken that for me!"

"Unite the cattle; quicken them for me," [he says]. Having placed the two cups on the *uttaravedi*, he touches the *uttaravedi* with his two thumbs, saying, "Thou art unassailable. They both walk around the *uttaravedi* in opposite directions, as if pushing it apart. The Adhvaryu goes around by the south, saying, "Begetting offspring rich in heroes, go around! O bright one, with thy bright luster! [The Pratiprasthātṛ goes around] saying, "Begetting offspring rich in progeny, go around!"

With the verse, "The churner [is] with the glow of the churner," the Pratiprasthātṛ [places the cup] to the north. The sacrificer touches the *śukra* cup with the formula, "United with Indra, may we overcome those who attack us. In front of the *uttaravedi*, they join the two cups together, or their forearms, with the formula: "Meeting from heaven and earth, [O arms], bestow life upon me; quicken that for me! Bestow the out-breath (*prāṇa*) upon me; quicken that for me! Bestow the in-breath (*apāna*) upon me; quicken that for me! Bestow the diffused breath (*vyāna*) upon me; quicken that for me!"

"Unite the eye; quicken it for me. Unite the ear; quicken it for me. Unite the mind; quicken it for me. Unite the speech; quicken it for me. Then the Adhvaryu addresses them both: "You two are life; bestow life upon me. Bestow life upon the sacrifice. Bestow life upon the lord of the sacrifice. You two are breath; bestow breath upon me. Bestow breath upon the sacrifice. Bestow breath upon the lord of the sacrifice."

You two are the eye; bestow the eye upon me. Bestow the eye upon the sacrifice. Bestow the eye upon the lord of the sacrifice. You two are the ear; bestow the ear upon me. Bestow the ear upon the sacrifice. Bestow the ear upon the lord of the sacrifice. 7.13.24

"O you two gods, Śukra and Manthin, arrange the divine clans; arrange the human clans. Bestow food and vigor upon our bodies; bestow vital breaths upon the cattle; bestow offspring upon me and upon the sacrificer. Having stepped forward from the east toward the west and having crossed over the *uttaravedi*, they cast away two unwatered wood-shavings outside the altar using that same mantra. Having touched water, they throw into the fire two watered [shavings]: the Adhvaryu with the formula, "Thou art the kindling-stick of Śukra."

"Thou art the fuel of the *manthin*," [says the Pratiprasthātṛ]. 3. The Camasādhvaryus stand behind with their goblets facing eastward. 4. Having called for the *āśrāvaṇa* and having received the response, he issues the command: "For the *Prātaḥsavana* of the bright, the *manthin*, the honey-dropping [Soma], announce the Soma-juices set forth for Indra! O Camasādhvaryus of the central performers, offer the oblations at the *vaṣaṭ* and the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*! O Camasādhvaryus of the Hotrakas, having offered once each, turn back after having drawn more of the *śukra*. 5. At the *vaṣaṭ* they offer. 6. The Adhvaryu and the Pratiprasthātṛ offer the *śukra* and the *manthin*.
He is the first fashioner, the maker of all; he is the first Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni;
he is the first wise Bṛhaspati. To him, O Indra, I offer the pressed [soma] with the cry of Svāhā!

Thus says the Adhvaryu. "To that Sūrya I offer the pressed [juice], svāhā!"—thus says the Pratiprasthātṛ. Some authorities prescribe that the Śukra and Manthin cups are accompanied by the *anuvapaṭkāra*; others prescribe them as being without the *anuvapaṭkāra*.

Then they perform the offerings again with the liquids drawn up. They are drawn from the *droṇakalaśa*. Taking the cup belonging to the Maitrāvaruṇa, the Adhvaryu steps across, calls for the *śrauṣaṭ*, and says, "O Praśāstṛ, recite the offering prayer! At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the offering. In this same sequence, whichever [priest] performs the sacrifice, to each one he gives the direction: "O Brahman, recite the offering prayer! O Potṛ, recite the offering prayer! O Neṣṭṛ, recite the offering prayer!"

"O Agnīdh, sacrifice!"—these [are the calls] for which these cups belong. (5) The *anuvaṣaṭkāra* is prescribed after all Soma offerings. (6) "The Agnīdh has sacrificed," thus the Hotṛ announces. (7) "He has performed a good deed; he will cause us to drink Soma," thus the Hotṛ replies. (8) He consecrates the portion with the mantra: "Consume! Come! Enter me! (9) He receives it with: "May I grasp you with the arms of the Aśvins. (10) He looks at it with: "O divine Soma, may I, being well-eyed, look upon you who are the observer of men. (11) Wherever...

And he should eat; in this very manner he should mutter these mantras. 12. Then, having invoked the invitation (*upahava*) for this [cup] and having applied it to his vital breaths (*prāṇa*), he eats with the mantra: "The delightful, victorious... 13. Whatever cups there may be that do not belong to Indra and are not *ārāśamsa* cups, this same mantra for eating applies to them at the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*). 14. Some recite universally: "May the goddess Vāc be satisfied with the Soma. 15. He eats the cup for Indra-Vāyu twice; the other two [cups] once each. He applies the cup for Mitra-Varuṇa to his eyes; he applies the cup for the Aśvins by moving it all around his ears. 16. 13.26.

The *hotṛ* eats first, then the *adhvaryu*, then the *pratiprasthātṛ*. (1) Whenever two or many may eat from a single vessel, the one who uttered the *vaṣaṭ* call must eat first. (2) Whosoever may eat at the same time, they should all invite one another by means of their ritual names. (3) The invitation consists of the address: "O so-and-so, invite me! and "I invite you, O so-and-so!"

The response is, "I am invited. (4) Having consumed [the portion], he touches himself with the formula, "Impel my limbs, O Lord of Bay Steeds. (5) Wherever he may consume [the Soma], he should touch himself in this very same manner. (6) Having consumed it, they do not release [the cup] until the pouring down [of the remnants]. (7) Having poured the residues of the two-deity cups into the Hotṛ’s goblet, he places a fragment of the cake into the vessel for Indra and Vāyu, and the curd-mixture (*payasyā*) into the vessel for Mitra and Varuṇa.

The parched grains (dhānā) belong to the Aśvins. 8. Then he places these [grains] behind the axle on the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart. 9. They remain thus set out until the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*). 10. Having performed the *niravadya* offering, he places the *iḍā* portion for the Hotṛ. 11. The Hotṛ invokes the *iḍā*. 12. They lift up the cups for him. 13. He holds the Hotṛ’s cup so that it touches [the others]. 14. When the *iḍā* has been invoked, they eat it, as they do in the archetype. 15. He places a fragment of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) for the Acchāvāka. 16.

The cup-holders consume [the Soma] according to their respective cups (yathācamasam). (17) For those who perform the central rites, [the formula is]: "O divine Soma, of thee belonging to the Vasumadgaṇa... (18) The consumption-mantra for the others is explained as being without reference to Indra. (19) The Hotṛ consumes from all the cups. (20) When they have been refilled again in all cases, the Adhvaryu [recites]: "A pleasant victory... (21) Whichever Adhvaryu should offer the oblation, he shall consume [the portion] facing the one who uttered the *vaṣaṭ* call. (22) Having consumed it, he causes it to swell [with the formula]: "Swell up; let it come together unto thee... (23) Wherever...

And he should cause it to swell; with this same [verse] he should cause it to swell. 24. The Nārāśamsa cups, having been caused to swell, settle beneath the southern Havirdhāna cart, below the support-beam (apālamba). 25. 13.27.

The Achāvāka sits down in front of his own *dhiṣṇiya* hearth outside the *sadas*. As he places a fragment of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) for him, [the Adhvaryu] says: "Achāvāka, speak what is to be spoken by you. When he recognizes [the verse]: "O Brahmins, call the Brahmins hither," then he says: "This Achāvāka desires an invitation; O Hotṛ, invite him. The Hotṛ invites him with a Ṛgvedic verse. When he recognizes [the verse]: "And our cows are invited; we are invited," then he says: "Recite for the cup being drawn."

Thus, having taken the cup of the Achāvāka that has been drawn out, having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Achāvāka, recite the offering prayer" (*achāvāka yaja*). (6) When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering. (7) He hands the portion for consumption to the Achāvāka. (8) The Achāvāka does not seek permission to consume from him. (9) He should not consume together with him. (10) If he should desire permission to consume from him, he should say to him, "Consume [it]. (11) Having consumed the Achāvāka’s cup and caused it to swell, he places it between the cups of the Neṣṭṛ and the Agnīdh. (12) Here, regarding the *savanīya* offerings...
He performs the oblations of the flour-smeared fragments and the husks (piṣṭalepaphalīkaraṇa). He releases the potsherds. At this point, some authorities prescribe the performance of the Vājina rite.

Then they proceed with the Ṛtu-cups. The Adhvaryu takes the southern Ṛtu-vessel, and the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the northern one. They draw the first two cups together and the last two together. The Adhvaryu draws [the first cup] with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art Madhu..."

"Thou art taken with a support; thou art Mādhava," [saying this] the Pratiprasthātṛ [takes his cup]. Having gone out, the Adhvaryu, having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, says, "Prompt for the season! (5). At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he offers the oblation. (6) The Adhvaryu turns back. (7) Having gone out, the Pratiprasthātṛ, having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, says, "Prompt for the season! (8). At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he offers the oblation. (9) They should not pass one another; they should cross only at the door. (10) The Adhvaryu enters by the southern side in the well-known manner.

It is well known that the Pratiprasthātṛ [takes the draught] from the north. As the Adhvaryu goes westward, the Pratiprasthātṛ receives him with a cup; as he goes eastward, [the Adhvaryu receives him] with a vessel. In this very manner they both take [the draughts] with each subsequent mantra: the Adhvaryu with each preceding one, and the Pratiprasthātṛ with each succeeding one. The Adhvaryu alone takes the thirteenth [draught] with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art a serpent; for Aṃhaspatya, thee! It is understood that twelve [draughts] are taken.

"Thirteen," say some; "fourteen," say others. (16) If thirteen are taken, they offer the first two together. (17) If fourteen, they offer the first two together and the last two together. (18) 13.29 The remainder of the previous [libations] he takes for the subsequent ones. (1) They are offered while not yet placed on the altar. (2) "Prompt with the Seasons!"—thus the Adhvaryu says three times; the Pratiprasthātṛ says three times. (3) Having turned the vessel around, "Prompt with the Seasons!"—thus the Adhvaryu says twice; the Pratiprasthātṛ says twice. (4) Having turned the vessel around, "Prompt with the Season!"—thus the Adhvaryu says once.

The Pratiprasthātṛ [acts] once. When he recognizes [the formula] "O two Adhvaryus, sacrifice," then the Adhvaryu says, "O Hotṛ, sacrifice this. When he recognizes [the formula] "O Gṛhapati, sacrifice," then the Sacrificer says, "O Hotṛ, sacrifice this. The seasonal cups (ṛtugrahas) are without the *anuvaṣaṭkāra*. The Pratiprasthātṛ pours the residue into the Adhvaryu’s cup.

The Adhvaryu [places the cup] in the Pratiprasthātṛ’s vessel; the Pratiprasthātṛ brings the portion for consumption with it. In this manner, they consume in succession, each for the one who sacrifices: with the formula "The delightful, overwhelming [cup]," the Adhvaryu [consumes] from the Hotṛ's [vessel]; the Pratiprasthātṛ from the Potṛ's; the Adhvaryu from the Neṣṭṛ's; the Pratiprasthātṛ from the Āgnīdhra's; the Adhvaryu from the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's; the Pratiprasthātṛ from the Maitrāvaruṇa's; the Adhvaryu from the Hotṛ's; and the Pratiprasthātṛ from the Potṛ's.

He draws the cup for Indra and Agni with the verse, "O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice" (RV 7.92.1). 1. The *śastra* (recitation) occurs here. 2. Having sat down in front of the Hotṛ, the Adhvaryu introduces the *śastra* with the remainder of the section beginning, "Iḍā, the invoker of the gods. 3. With this very [formula], he introduces all the *śastras*. 4. Then, while he is sitting facing away with his knees raised, the Hotṛ calls out to him. 5. [The Adhvaryu] turns clockwise with the words, "Śauṃsā modīva. 6. Grasping the *ṛtupātra*, standing upright, he responds (*pratigṛṇāti*) in the *sadas*.

7. Or he may respond while bowing low. 8. At the half-verses, [he responds] with "Othā moda iva. 9. At the *praṇava*s (the concluding syllables), [he responds] with "Omothā moda iva. 10. He should not respond by omitting the half-verse. 11. Wherever the Hotṛ pauses, he should simply say, "Omothā moda iva. 12. In the *vyāhāva* (the call for response), he performs both: "Śauṃsā moda iva" and "Othā moda iva. 13. He pronounces the *praṇava* together with the final *praṇava* of the concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*). 14. In this very manner he responds to all the *śastra*s, except for the beginning of the cup-offering (*pātrārambhaṇa*).

He consecrates the sacrificial vessel with the formula, "Of the vessel, you are the vessel" (ŚB 4.2.1.15). With this very formula, he consecrates all the vessels (16). Having swallowed the sacrificial vessel, the Adhvaryu takes up the cup; they take up the Nārāśamsa goblets (17). Having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice to Soma" (18). When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation (19). 13.31.

They cause the *nārāśamsa* cups to vibrate following both the *vaṣaṭ*-call and the subsequent *anuvaṣaṭ*-call. 1. The mantra for consuming the cup dedicated to Indra has already been explained. 2. They consume the *nārāśamsa* cups with the formula: "O God Soma, of thee who hast been drunk by Narāśamsa... 3. In this very manner, at each pressing (*savana*), they consume the *nārāśamsa* cups using each successive *nārāśamsa*. 4. Having consumed them all, they cause them to swell. 5. The swelling and the setting down have already been explained. 6. He draws the *vaiśvadeva* cup with the *śukra* vessel.

With this *anuvāka*, "O you who protect from distress, supporters of men" (RV 8.69.1 ff.), the *stotra* and *śastra* are performed here. Having responded to the *śastra*, the Adhvaryu takes up the cup; they take up the *nārāśamsa* goblets. Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice to Soma. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation. The procedure for the shaking has been explained. The mantra for the consumption of the cup has been explained. The procedure for the *nārāśamsas* has been explained. They consume all [the portions]; they do not cause them to swell.

They cleanse themselves. 15. From this point onward, the cups at the morning pressing are for those who consume all [the soma]. 16. Thereupon, he draws out the Ukthya. 17. He takes a third portion from the Ukthya-vessel into the Ukthya-cup with the formula: "Thou art taken with a support; for Mitra and Varuṇa, thee! 18. Then he sets it down with the formula: "This is thy womb; for Mitra and Varuṇa, thee! 19. With the formula "Thou art the oblation again," he touches the vessel. 20. He pours the draughts into the cups, having the cup belonging to the Maitrāvaruṇa as the chief. 21. At the Stotra and Śastra...

Here, having cast aside his sacrificial knife, the Adhvaryu takes up the cup; the Camasādhvaryus take up their goblets. Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice the Soma-draughts. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, they offer. Into the Maitrāvaruṇa’s goblet, the Adhvaryu pours the residue, saying, "I fill thee, who art desirous of the gods, for the gods, for the life of the sacrifice. 13.32

If the Adhvaryu should desire, "May I endow myself with the glory of the sacrifice," he proceeds as prescribed in the traditional text: "The cup-bearers consume [the Soma] from their respective cups with the formula, 'The pleasant, overpowering... (RV 8.91.2). In this manner, the Pratiprasthātṛ proceeds without consuming [the Soma] during the two subsequent Ukthya-vigrahas. Into whichever cup is the principal one, into each of those he pours the residue. The cup of the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is the second principal one.

The third [cup] has the Achāvāka’s cup as its chief. By this, the sequence of the *śastra* recitations and the *yājyā* verses is explained. This much is the difference: for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin, the drawing and setting down of the cup are performed with the formula "Indra, thee"; the consumption mantra is addressed to Indra. For the Achāvāka, the drawing and setting down of the cup are performed with the formula "Indra and Agni, thee."

"Sweet, overcoming"—this is the mantra for the consumption. (7) Having taken the final Ukthya vessel, he does not touch the pot. (8) Having set down the Ukthya pot, he draws the Ṣoḍaśin cup with this Anuvāka beginning "Mount the chariot, O slayer of Vṛtra," or with the subsequent one. (9) Or rather, he may draw it as the last of the stream-cups (dhārāgraha). (10) In this very manner, at each pressing, he draws the Ṣoḍaśin with the subsequent Anuvāka. (11) Having drawn the Ṣoḍaśin, he issues the command: "Fill up the cups; O Droṇakalaśa..."

Pour the *ṇakalaśa* into the *pūtabhṛt*; pour all the *rājāna* [Soma] into the cups; having wiped the two jars with the fringes of the filter, turn them upside down—thus [he says]. 12. Having responded to the morning pressing with "O reciter of the *uktha*," 13. and having offered the oblation with "May Agni protect us at the morning pressing," he issues the command: "O *praśāstṛ*, give the impulse! 14. "Proceed! says the *praśāstṛ*. 15. The morning pressing is concluded. 16. 13.33. Thus ends the thirteenth chapter. Now begins the fourteenth chapter.

We shall explain the midday pressing (mādhyaṃdina-savana). Its ritual procedure (kalpa) has been explained by that of the morning pressing (prātaḥsavana). We shall enumerate the modifications (vikāra). Then he issues the command: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, pour out the sacrificial grains for the Savanīya offerings. Having filled the Hotṛ’s cup with the Vasatīvarī waters, he makes the sacrificer recite the Nigrābhya formulas as at the morning pressing. Having placed the entire King Soma upon the pressing-skin, he gives the turban to the Grāvastut. Even without being commanded, [the Grāvastut recites] the Grāvastotrīyā verses.

He recites [the verses]. 7. They press the great pressing (mahābhiṣava) just as at the morning pressing. 8. This much is different: they press [saying], "Hither for him! Hither for him! 9. At the middle round of the final pressing, they press [saying], "The Great One (bṛhat)! 10. Then, as if seeking to win favor, they press the final round [saying], "Hither for him! Hither for him! Hither for him! 11. When the King [Soma] has been pressed during the final round, he remains uncollected; then the Pratiprasthātṛ pays homage to the pressing-stones [with the verse]: "O gods, O pressing-stones, Indu, Indra..."

Thus they spoke. They have driven Indra hither from the furthest distance, from this common dwelling-place, from the vast intermediate space. They have pressed out prosperity for us; they have pressed out spiritual splendor for me. In battle, they have struck down the demons.

"Struck down is the oppressor of the Brahmin"—this is the formula. (12) It is the same up to the time of the drawing of the cups. (13) He draws the *śukra* and *manthin* first. (14) He draws the *āgrayaṇa* from three streams. (15) Having poured the King [Soma] which was in the *āgrayaṇa* vessel into another vessel, he makes it the second stream; from the *udacana* [ladle], he makes the third. (16) Having drawn the *ukthya* according to the procedure for the *ukthya*, (17) 14.1.

He draws the two Marutvatīya cups with two ṛtu-vessels: the first with the Adhvaryu’s vessel using [the verse] "The bull accompanied by the Maruts, increasing in strength"; the second with the Pratiprasthātṛ’s vessel using [the verse] "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here. He pours out from the Droṇakalaśa as much of the King (Soma) as he considers sufficient for the midday pressing. This procedure is the same up to the Pavamāna laud. Bending forward and facing westward, they proceed toward the midday Pavamāna; its metre is Triṣṭubh and its deity is the Rudras.

"May we reach safety by means of the wolf, by a path that has no rival; O Rudras, may we attain it. And [he recites]: "May Speech, going at the head, go at the front. (4) Having gone around the north of the two *havirdhāna* sheds and the south of the *mārjālīya*, and having entered the *sadas* by the eastern door, the Adhvaryu stands in front of the *hotrīya* shed. The others pass beyond the *praśāstrīya* shed. (5) They chant the midday *pavamāna* stotra. (6) While it is being chanted, the sacrificer mutters the *anvāroha* formula: "You are the fair-winged eagle, having the *triṣṭubh* as your metre. (7) [The procedure] is the same up to the formal command (*saṃpraiṣa*). (8) Here he does not urge the animal forward, nor does he worship the King Soma.

"O Pratiprasthātṛ, follow with the curd-mixture (dadhigharma)!"—with these words he inclines toward the end of the formal command (saṃpraiṣa). 9. This is the same up to the pouring out (nirvapaṇa) of the Savanīya offerings. 10. Intending to pour out the Savanīya offerings, he pours out the animal-cake (paśupuroḍāśa) for Agni in the Agniṣṭoma; for Indra-Agni as the second in the Ukthya; for Indra as the third in the Ṣoḍaśin; and for Sarasvatī as the fourth in the Atirātra. 11. After that, he pours out the Savanīya offerings. 12. This much is different.

In the two latter pressings, there is a *payasyā* (curd-mixture). 13. The offering of the *savanīya* oblations, the spreading of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the decoration, the recitation for the cups (*graha-avakāśa*), and the creeping forward (*sarpaṇa*) have been explained. 14. He proceeds with the *dadhigharma* (the hot milk mixed with curds). 15. In a ladle made of *udumbara* wood, he takes the curds upon the *āgnīdhrīya* fire-altar with the verse: "As great as heaven and earth are in their greatness... 16. 14.2.

Then he places it over the Āgnīdhra fire with the formula: "May speech and mind cook you; may out-breath and in-breath cook you; may sight and hearing cook you; may skill and strength cook you; may vigor and force cook you; may life-span and old age cook you; may the self and the body cook you. You are cooked; you have been made cooked."

"For thee that art cooked, for those that are cooked," [he says]. Then he issues the command: "O Hotṛ, speak what is to be spoken by thee. When he recognizes [the verse]: "If it is cooked, offer; if it is not cooked, wait," then he says: "The oblation is cooked. Having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "Recite the offering prayer (*yāja*) for the Dadhi-gharma. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers: "Him whom they call Indra, him whom they call Varuṇa; him whom they call Mitra, him whom they call Truth; he who is the most divine among the gods, born of fervor—for him, for them, svāhā!"

Thus, when the second *anuvaṣaṭ* has been uttered, having offered the second portion, he leaves a remnant. Those who are entitled to the *pravargya* consume that; for this, there is a consumption mantra from the *araṇye'nuvākyas*. Another view is that the *dadhigharma* does not exist when there is no *pravargya*. Then he sets out the *savanīya* offerings. Having proceeded with the animal-cake (*paśupuroḍāśa*), he proceeds with the *savanīya* offerings. This much is different: [at this point] he says, "Recite the invitatory verse for the cakes of Indra for the midday pressing."

"O Hotṛ, give the call for the sacrificial cakes set forth for Indra at the midday pressing," he thus commands. (11) For all the animal-cake offerings, the *sviṣṭakṛt* oblation is the same, as is the *praisha* and the *iḍā*. (12) According to another view, there is no animal-cake offering for the *savanīya* sacrifice. (13) He pours the contents of the *ādhavanīya* vessel into the *pūtabhṛt* vessel. (14) Everything is the same up to the formal command (*saṃpraiṣa*). (15) This much is different.

"Of the portion belonging exclusively to the midday pressing, accompanied by the *śukra* cup, the *manthin* cup, and dripping with honey"—this is the beginning of the formal call (*saṃpraiṣa*). (16) It is the same up to the cups being refilled. (17) The *achāvāka* priest performs the *saṃyaja* offering before the *āgnīdhra*. (18) Here, one does not place a fragment of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa-śakala*) for the *achāvāka*. (19) The cup-holders consume [the Soma] according to their respective cups. (20) "O God Soma, of thee who art the leader of Rudra’s troop"—this very formula for consumption (*bhakṣamantra*) is used at the midday pressing, except in other cases.
[They offer] to the *nārāśamsa* cups. (21) Having consumed them all, they cause them to swell. (22) The swelling and the setting down have been explained. (23) 14.3

When the *nārāśamsa* cups have been consumed, having gone around to the north of the *havirdhāna* shed, the north of the *āgnīdhrīya* fire, and the north of the *sadas*, he enters the *vamśa* by the eastern door. Having sat down behind the *śālāmukhīya* fire and having taken four spoonfuls of clarified butter into the *juhū* ladle, he ties a piece of gold with a *niṣṭarkya* knot using a blade of *darbha* grass and places it [into the ladle]. (1) The summoning of the attendants, the simultaneous grasping [of the hands], and the covering [of the head] have been explained in the context of the *vaisarjana* offerings. (2) Having brought the edge of the cloth near the handle of the ladle...

He offers the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*). With the two verses, "Upwards that" (*udu tyam*) and "The bright one" (*citram*), he offers into the *gārhapatya* fire. Having taken another fourfold portion of clarified butter, he offers the gold while saying, "Go to heaven, fly to the light," and then holds it up. Then these sacrificial gifts stand to the south of the altar: twelve hundred cows, sesame seeds, beans, boiled rice, a stirred drink (*mantha*), a goat, a sheep, a garment, gold, a chariot, a horse, an elephant, and a man. According to some, there are twenty-one [of each].

"Twenty-four," say some; "an unlimited number," say others; "the entirety of all one's possessions," say others. (7) Holding gold and clarified butter, the sacrificer approaches the sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇā*), saying: "By means of your form I approach my own form; by means of your vital strength I approach my own vital strength. (8) With the words, "May Tutha, the all-knowing, distribute you," he steps into the middle. (9) Then, having made them tremble with a black antelope skin and having either divided them or not divided them, he brings them forward along the front of the *prāgvam̐śa* shed and between the *sadas* and the *antareṇa*.

[He takes] those [waters] for the Neṣṭṛ and the Agnīdhra. 10. He pours them out northward between the Cātvāla pit and the Agnīdhra’s altar. 11. While they are being carried across, he addresses the Āhavanīya fire with the mantra beginning, "This wealth of thine, O Agni, comes, distilling Soma," and ending with, "leading us by the path of the sacrifice to prosperity. 12. 14.4.

The Āgnīdhra offers this clarified butter with the verse, "O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth" (RV 1.189.1). He should offer with the second verse addressed to Varuṇa, "In the forests he has stretched out the atmosphere," if a chariot, a horse, or even a garment is to be given. He should offer with the third verse addressed to Prajāpati, if he intends to give an elephant or a man. He gives gold to the first Ātreya, according to some; to the middle one, according to others; and to the last one, according to others, with the formula: "May I today prosper as a Brāhmaṇa, a seer, and a descendant of seers."

If he does not find one who is an Ātreya or a well-disposed descendant of a Ṛṣi, he should give it to him. First, he gives a cushion with its entire thread-wool to the Āgnīdhra, as well as a goat. Then, he should give to the Brahman a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) such that he does not exceed the prescribed rule; he should give in this manner. Then [he gives] to the Udgātṛs and the Hotṛs. To the Adhvaryus, however, while they are seated in the Havirdhāna shed. Finally, he gives to the Pratihartṛ. Half [of the fee] to those entitled to half, a third to those entitled to a third, and a quarter to those entitled to a quarter.

These have been explained in the context of the twelve-day sacrifice (dvādaśāha). Having given to the officiating priests (ṛtvij), he gives to the attendants (prasarpaka). These sit down within the *sadas* to the south of the *pṛṣṭhyā*-line. He gives to one who belongs to a different *ṛṣi*-lineage (*nānārṣeya*) and is learned; not to one who does not belong to an *ṛṣi*-lineage even if he is learned; he gives only to one who belongs to an *ṛṣi*-lineage and is learned. He does not give to those of the Kaṇva or Kaśyapa lineages, nor to a kinsman, nor to one who has already received his share, nor to one who is afraid, nor to one who is begging.

"It is known from scripture: 'That sacrificial gift (dakṣiṇā) which one gives to a petitioner goes to him. (15) One gives the sacrificial gift to a Brāhmaṇa who is learned in the Vedas (śrotriya) while he is seated within the sacrificial altar-ground (antarvedi). (16) It may also be given to a non-Brāhmaṇa who possesses knowledge. (17) 14.5 If another person should not desire the gift being given, one should give that sacrificial gift, along with other wealth, to someone whom one hates. (1) From whom should one give to these [others]? "From this very twelve-hundred-fold [sacrifice]," says one school. (2)

"Look elsewhere"—this is another [instruction]. "Behold the heaven, behold the mid-region"—with these words he should look toward the *sadas*. He consecrates the led-in sacrificial gifts (*dakṣiṇās*) with the remainder of the section beginning, "Going to the gods, go from us as givers. In the *āgnīdhra* shed, he offers the *vaiśvakarman* oblations with the five verses beginning, "The seers have accused the lord of the sacrifice of sin. He throws the black antelope horn into the *cātvāla* pit with [the verse]: "On the head of the swiftly moving deer is the remedy; with the horn, he has destroyed the disease that spreads in all directions, securing a good field."

The deer, the golden-hued beast, has followed you with its four feet. O horn, loosen this knot: that which is knotted in his ankle, that which is knotted in his heart, and that which is knotted in his mind.

With these two [verses], he then issues the command: "Recite for Indra accompanied by the Maruts. When the recitation for Indra accompanied by the Maruts has been completed, then no offering is made until the oblation of the *ānūbandhya* victim's omentum. The Adhvaryu takes the portion previously drawn, and the Pratiprasthātṛ takes the subsequent one. Having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "Prompt the call for Indra accompanied by the Maruts! At the utterance of the *vaṣaṭ*, they both offer. Some authorities prescribe that the two *marutvatīya* offerings are accompanied by the *anuvaṣaṭ*; others say they are without the *anuvaṣaṭ*.

Some [perform] the subsequent *vaṣaṭ*-call; 12. they both pour out [the remnants] according to the seasons, as in the case of the cups (*graha*); 13. they consume [the draughts] by means of the Pratiprasthātṛ. 14. Having set down the vessel right here, the Adhvaryu takes the final Marutvatīya cup with his own vessel and the residue, [reciting]: "O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, a bull for the battle... 15. The *śastra* (recitation) occurs here. 16. He responds to the *śastra* while holding the seasonal cup (*ṛtupātra*). 17. Having responded to the *śastra*, the Adhvaryu takes up the cup.

They take up the *nārāśamsa* cups. (18) Having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice the *soma*! (19) When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering. (20) The procedure for the shaking [of the cups] has been explained. (21) The mantra for consuming the cup has been explained. (22) The procedure for the *nārāśamsas* has been explained. (23) Without having consumed them all, they cause them to swell. (24) The swelling and the setting down have been explained. (25) 14.6

He draws the Māhendra cup with the Śukra vessel using this Anuvāka beginning with "Great is Indra who by his might," or with the following one. 1. The Stotra and Śastra belong here. 2. Having introduced the Stotra, he issues the command: "O pressers, press the Soma; sound the mortars; O Āgnīdh, bring the milk-mixture (āśira); attend to the Soma-rite. 3. Here he should perform the pressing for the third extraction (tārtīyasavanīya). He should offer the Savanīya cakes and the Soma-oblation, and he should bring the milk-mixture; this is one view.

"In the third pressing"—this is another [instruction]. Having responded to the *śastra*, the Adhvaryu takes up the cup; they take up the *nārāśamsa* cups; they take up the *atigrāhya* cups. Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice to Soma. When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation. The procedure for the shaking has been explained. Then they offer the *atigrāhya* cups with these mantras, according to their respective forms: "O Agni, full of splendor... The mantra for the consumption of the cup has been explained. Then they consume the *atigrāhya* cups with [the mantra]: "In me wisdom, in me..."

With these mantras, beginning with "prajāṃ," [the cups] are consumed according to their respective forms. 11. The procedure for the *nārāśaṃsa* cups has been explained. 12. They consume all [of them]. 13. They do not cause them to swell. 14. They perform the ritual purification (*mārjana*). 15. From this point onward, at the midday pressing (*mādhyaṃdina*), the cups are indeed for total consumption (*sarvabhakṣa*). 16. Thereafter, he draws the *ukthya* cup as was done at the morning pressing. 17. This much is different: [he recites] "indrā ya tvā."

The two formulas for drawing and setting down the cup are "indrā ya tvā" (VS 7.34) everywhere. 17. The *bhakṣa*-mantra belongs to Indra. 18. At that very time, he draws the *ṣoḍaśin* cup. 19. Having drawn the *ṣoḍaśin*, he issues the call: "Fill the cups to the brim; pour the *droṇakalaśa* into the *pūtabhṛt*; pour the entire *rājā* (Soma) into the cups; having wiped the two jars with the fringes, turn them face down. 20. Having responded to the midday pressing, he says, "The hymn has been recited. 21. [The deities are] the Viśve Devas, the Maruts, and Indra.

Having offered the oblation with the verse beginning "asmān," he issues the direction: "O Praśāstṛ, give the command! 22. The Praśāstṛ says, "Proceed! 23. The midday pressing (mādhyaṃdina-savana) concludes. 24. 14.7.

We shall now explain the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*). (1) When many [priests] should be within the sacrificial ground (*antarvedi*), then one should draw the Āditya cup. (2) If one whose rival is performing the Soma sacrifice should draw the Āditya cup, he should stand outside the sacrificial ground for as long as that Āditya cup is being drawn. (3) If his rival should have already entered [the sacrificial ground], he should draw the Āditya cup while remaining within the sacrificial ground. (4) Having closed the doors of the two *havirdhāna* sheds, he draws the third portion from the Āditya vessel into the Āditya cup with these three verses beginning, "Never indeed art thou barren" (*kadā cana starīr asi*). (5) He draws the Soma first, and then...

One should mix the curds with the heated Soma. It is known from scripture: "With a *triṣṭubh* verse, he takes the curds in the middle. With the formula, "I mix thee with that which is divine rain," one should mix it with curds on top for one who desires rain; one should not take the curds in the middle. Having placed the *ādityasthālī* (the vessel for the Āditya cup) in its place like a broth, he places the *upām̐śusavana* stone into the cup with the formula, "O Vivasvat Āditya, this is thy draught of Soma. Having lifted it up, he attains the realization.

If the drop should fall immediately, Parjanya will be rainy; if it does not rain for a long time, he will be dry. Without setting down the cup, the Adhvaryu takes it up and stands, saying: "May the god Sūrya protect me from the gods. Then he issues the command: "Recite the invitatory verse for the Ādityas, who are dear, whose abodes are dear, whose vows are dear, the lords of the great year, the overseers of the wide mid-region. 14.8.10–11.

The sacrificer takes hold of the Āditya [stone], saying: "I from above, I from below. (1) He causes it to move with *darbha* grass, saying: "From the ocean, from the intermediate space. (2) Having covered it with *darbha* grass, he steps out, saying: "The sage extends the path of the sacrifice. (3) Having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "Prompt [the Hotṛ] for the dear Ādityas, who have dear abodes, dear vows, who are the lords of the great dwelling-place, the overseers of the wide intermediate space! (4) He throws the *darbha* grass into the fire, saying: "Those which are all yours..."

With the verse, "O Agni, there are fuel-sticks for thee," he offers at the *vaṣaṭ*-call while looking away; he does not perform the *anuvaṣaṭ*-call, nor should he look back after having offered. For one who desires rain, he should offer with the verse, "Make the earth swell. Having placed the Aditya-vessel, which contains clarified butter, in its proper place, he issues the command: "O Pratiprasthātṛ, pour out the *savanīya* oblations. Having filled the Hotṛ’s cup with the *vasatīvarī* waters, he makes the sacrificer recite over the *nigrābhya* waters as was done at the morning pressing. [He takes] from the *upaṃśu* vessel...

Having poured the dregs into the *śumṛjīṣa* vessel, they perform the great pressing (*mahābhiṣava*) just as at the morning pressing. (11) It is the same up to the time for drawing the cups. (12) Here, one does not draw the *śukra* and *manthin* cups. (13) One draws the *āgrayaṇa* cup from four streams. (14) Having poured that King [Soma] which is in the *āgrayaṇa* vessel into another vessel, he makes it the second stream; from the *āditya* cup, the third; and from the *āditya* vessel, the fourth. (15) 14.9

He draws the Ukthya cup according to the procedure for the Ukthya, if there is an Ukthya-stotra. The sacrificer and his wife churn the *āśira* (milk-mixture) in the Āgnīdhra fire-shed; some say that the wife alone churns the *āśira*. The sacrificer enters by the eastern door.

With another wife he causes her to step forward. Having performed that which precedes the Pavamāna cups, the sacrificer, together with his wife, pours the *āśira* milk into the *pūtabhṛt* vessel with these four verses beginning, "O gods, look upon us for the sake of beauty. It is the same up to the Pavamāna [laud]. Bending backward and stooping, they creep toward the Ārbhava Pavamāna; the path is Jāgata, the deity is the Ādityas, [thinking], "By the path that is not too narrow, may I safely reach the Ādityas."

And [he recites]: "May speech go at the head; may it go at the head. (6) His movement during the Mādhyandina Pavamāna has been explained. (7) While the chant is being performed, the sacrificer mutters the *anvāroha* formula: "Thou art the *saghā*, having the *jagatī* as thy metre. (8) [The procedure] is the same up to the *saṃpraiṣa*. (9) At the end of the *saṃpraiṣa*, "O Pratiprasthātṛ, converse regarding the animal sacrifice," he bows down. (10) [The procedure] is the same up to the distribution of the *dhiṣṇiya* hearths. (11) He distributes the flaming *dhiṣṇiya* hearths by means of wooden sticks (*śalākā*). (12) 14.10

We shall explain the sprinkling from above (upariṣṭād-vyāghāraṇa). Or rather, one may perform that [sprinkling] at that very same place. The offering of the *savanīya* oblations, the spreading of the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), the decoration, the standing for the invitation to the cups (*grahāvakāśa*), and the creeping forward have been explained. One proceeds with the animal sacrifice ending with the *iḍā*. This [animal sacrifice] is performed at all the pressings, or at the third pressing alone. Having proceeded with the animal sacrifice, one proceeds with the *savanīya* oblations. This much is the difference.

"Recite the invitatory verse for the rice-cakes for Indra at the third pressing. Having thus issued the command, "Prompt the offering for the rice-cakes set forth for Indra at the third pressing," he gives the *saṃpraisha*. The *sviṣṭakṛt* oblation has been explained; likewise the *iḍā*. He pours the contents of the *ādhavanīya* vessel into the *pūtabhṛt*. Everything is the same up to the *saṃpraisha*, except for this much.

Taking up the Hotṛ’s cup, he issues the preliminary command: "O Agnīdh, give the impulse for the Somas set forth for Indra—Somas that are abundant, pervasive, powerful, all-encompassing, endowed with vigor, accompanied by Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, and the Viśve Devas, and which are strong and mixed with milk! (11) At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, they offer the oblation, saying: "To the flying eagle, *svāhā*! (12) At the subsequent *vaṣaṭ* call, they offer a second time, saying: "*Vaṭ*! Homage to him who is self-praised! (13) It is exactly thus.

He offers each subsequent oblation with each subsequent of the following two mantras for those [portions] that have been drawn up again (punarabhyunnīta). (14) He consecrates all the offered portions with the mantra: "May they be satiated by the honey and the ghee of the Hotṛ-offerings. (15) [The ritual] is the same up to the consumption [of the remnants]. (16) He places pieces of the sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa-śakala) there for the purpose of setting them down. (17) The participants of the goblets (camasins) consume [the remnants] according to their respective goblets.

"O God Soma, [partake] of the cup belonging to the Ādityas,"—this indeed is the *bhakṣa-mantra* at the third pressing, except for the *nārāśamsa* cups. (18) They observe both types of deities when the cups have been refilled. (19) Having consumed them all, they cause them to swell. (20) The swelling and the setting down have been explained. (21) 14.11

Each person pours [the remnants] into his own cup; they place three pieces of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) into each [cup]. These mantras, beginning with the offering and ending with the dismissal, are recited as in the *Piṇḍapitṛyajña*: "This for you, father, and for those who follow you," and so forth. One view is that they should offer these to their own paternal grandfathers.

The sacrificer himself should mutter the mantras, while the others should set down the vessels silently; this is another view. (3) He draws the Sāvitra cup from the Āgrayaṇa vessel with the Antaryāma vessel, using this section beginning with "vāmam adya savitar. (4) He does not set it down. (5) Then he issues the command: "Recite for the god Savitṛ. (6) Having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says: "Prompt for the god Savitṛ. (7) When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he makes the offering.

He does not perform the *anuvaṣaṭ* call. Into that *saṃsrāva* vessel, he draws the *vaiśvadeva* cup from the *pūtabhṛt* jar, [saying]: "Thou art taken with a support; thou art good protection, thou art a firm foundation. (9) A *śastra* recitation occurs here. (10) When he recognizes [the verse]: "With one and with ten, O self-existent one," then the *pratiprasthātṛ*, having washed the cups for the dual deities, places them on the mound (*khara*). (11) When he recognizes [the verse]: "To Heaven and Earth, who increase the cosmic order through sacrifices," then he responds with the *anyataratomoda* chant, [singing] "madā... (12)

"Moda iva uttha moda iva"—[the Adhvaryu recites] up to this point of the *āvyāhāva*. (12) Having responded to the *śastra*, the Adhvaryu takes up the cup; they take up the *nārāśamsa* goblets. (13) Having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says: "O reciter of the *uktha*, sacrifice the Soma! (14) When the *vaṣaṭ* is uttered, he offers the oblation. (15) The procedure for the shaking [of the cups] has been explained. (16) He modifies the formula for consuming the cup to read: "Of that which was drunk by the deities Savitṛ and Viśve-devās. (17) The procedure for the *nārāśamsas* has been explained. (18) They consume all [the cups]; they do not cause them to swell. (19)
They cleanse themselves. 20. From this point onwards, at the third pressing, the cups are indeed for all to consume. 21. 14.12.

Then he offers the *saumya* oblation, either together with the *savanīya* offerings. Having set it down and taken the clarified butter as it was drawn, having stepped across and called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "Recite the offering prayer for the clarified butter. At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he makes the offering. Sitting right there, having placed the sacred thread over his right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*), he cuts off the first portion of the *saumya* with his hand and the second with the stirring-spoon (*mekṣaṇa*). Having sprinkled it with butter and stepped across toward the north, having called for the *āśrāvaṇa*, he says, "Recite the offering prayer for the *saumya*. At the *vaṣaṭ*-call, he makes the offering in the southern half. Sitting right there, having placed the sacred thread over his left shoulder (*yajñopavīta*)...

Having touched water and taken the clarified butter as it was originally drawn, having stepped across and called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "Recite the offering prayer for the clarified butter" (*ghṛtasya yaja*). At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he makes the oblation. Some authorities prescribe that the circumambulatory offering (*parījyā*) of the *saumya* [caru] takes place on either side. They carry the *caru*, having filled it with clarified butter, to the Udgātṛs. They gaze upon it, saying, "This is yours; that which is yours here. If he has not yet passed away, he gazes back at it.

If he should be dead, one should look at him with [the verse]: "That mind of mine which has gone away... (RV 10.58.1). It is known from the tradition that this [grain] is to be eaten by one who is ill, by one desiring food, and by one who, though capable of eating, does not eat; by such a person it is to be eaten. Having taken nine portions of clarified butter into the *juhū* ladle, he sprinkles it over the flaming hearths (*dhiṣṇiya*). Having set aside the residue of the sprinkling, he draws the *pātnīvata* cup from the *āgrayaṇa* vessel with the *upāṃśu* vessel, saying: "Thou art taken with a support; O Soma (*indo*), of thee pressed by Bṛhaspati, [I take] the power (*indriya*)."

15. "As many cups as I draw for the one accompanied by the wives (pātnīvata)," [he says]. Having performed the pouring of the sprinkling-water, having stepped across, and having called for the *śrauṣaṭ*, he says, "O Agnīdh, recite the offering prayer (*yaja*) for the cup for the one accompanied by the wives. 16. At the utterance of *vaṣaṭ*, he offers with the remainder of the section beginning, "O Agni, accompanied by the wives! 17. Some prescribe the cup for the one accompanied by the wives (*pātnīvata*) with a subsequent *vaṣaṭ* call (*sānuvaṣaṭkāra*), while others prescribe it without a subsequent *vaṣaṭ* call (*ananuvaṣaṭkāra*). According to some, he utters the *upāṃśu* (inaudible) *vaṣaṭ* call. 18. 14.13.

While taking the portion for consumption, he issues the command: "O Agnīdh, sit in the lap of the Neṣṭṛ; O Neṣṭṛ, lead up the wife; O Unnetṛ, pour out the cups beginning with the Hotṛ’s cup; make room for the Dhruva vessel in the Hotṛ’s cup; pour out the entire Soma-king into the cups; having wiped the two jars with the fringes of the cloth, turn them face down; O Udgātṛ, have the wife count [the drops]; let the water flow forth. 1. They perform according to what was commanded. 2. Having stepped between the Neṣṭṛ and the Dhiṣṇiya hearth, the Agnīdh consumes [his portion].

He modifies the *bhakṣa*-mantra for that which has been drunk by Agni. Having caused the hearths (*dhiṣṇiya*) to blaze up, he introduces the *yajñāyajñīya* stotra. The officiating priests and the sacrificer have their ears covered; they show their navels like those of sheep. The *udgātṛ* causes the *patnī* to count the *hiṅkāra* of the *udgātṛ* against three *stotriya* verses with the verse: "Of thee, the all-possessing, the all-favoring, the bull-strong. Having bared her right thigh, the *patnī* [counts] the *pannejana* waters against three [verses].

He causes [the vessels] to flow forward with the anuvāka beginning with *agan devān*. With the verse containing the word *viṣṇu*, he causes them to flow toward the groin. He causes them to flow either eastward or northward; according to some, both eastward and northward. When the *stotra* has been concluded, he introduces the *śastra*. When he recognizes the words, "Truly this is sweet, and this is honeyed," he responds with the *pratigara* on both sides: "madā moda iva, modā moda iva," until the *vyāhāva*. When he recognizes the words, "And may Ahi Budhnya hear us," in this verse addressed to the Viśvedevas...

When the *paridhānīyā* verse is being recited, or once it has been recited, the Pratiprasthātṛ, intending to pour the *dhruva* cup into the Hotṛ’s goblet, stands near it with the formula: "Thou art existence; place me in existence. (11) Then he grasps it with both hands with the formula: "I grasp thee for Heaven and Earth. (12) He carries it forward with the formula: "May all the gods, the Vaiśvānaras, cause thee to move forth. (13–14) 14.14
